subject: Post-demo recap — Dedicated capacity integration: technical asks & workbook
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@quanticahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap — Dedicated capacity integration: technical asks & workbook

Thanks again for the demo today, Evan — appreciate the time. Quick recap from our side and a concise list of asks so we can size Dedicated capacity and plan the technical deep-dive. I’ve attached a workbook (dedicated_capacity_workbook.xlsx) to capture the numbers below — if you can drop answers into the green cells we’ll convert them into a concrete sizing recommendation and cost estimate.

High-level summary (from today's call)
- Goal: embed LLM-powered summarization + assisted triage into Quantica’s clinician triage flow (low-latency generation + reranking).
- Primary concerns: P99 latency, predictable throughput during peak hours, data residency & auth/KMS model.

Tech/Integration items we need filled out
1) SDK & auth
  - Primary SDK language(s) you’ll use (e.g., python/node/java): please list versions.
  - Preferred auth pattern: API key (tenant-managed) vs mTLS vs our KMS-integration? (we can support multiple patterns; KMS/HSM options require slightly different onboarding).
2) Routing & model selection
  - Single model (high-accuracy) or split path (fast/cheap vs high-quality fallback)? Any constraints on failover to lower-capacity regions?
3) Structured output & tool calling
  - Will you use function/tool-calling for deterministic extraction (e.g., JSON schema) and external tool invocations? If so, include example schemas/requirements in the workbook or paste a sample snippet.
4) Embeddings & reranker
  - Estimated embedding writes per minute and expected QPS for reranker. Are you planning an async embedding pipeline or inline calls from the app?
5) Traffic profile & sizing (important for Dedicated)
  - Peak requests per minute (RPS) and average tokens per request (input + expected output).
  - Target concurrency (simultaneous generation sessions).
  - Reranker/embedding concurrency separate from generation? If so, approximate separation.
6) Autoscaling & queues
  - Acceptable cold-start window for autoscale (how long can queues buffer requests).
  - Maximum queue depth and SLA for queued requests (e.g., 5s window, 20s window).

Ask: Please fill the attached workbook by EOD Friday (2026-09-10). Once we have those numbers Marissa (solutions engineering) and I will produce: a) recommended GPU pool sizing, b) autoscale policy suggestions (warm pool vs on-demand), and c) an initial SLA draft.

Next steps we propose
- Evan: fill workbook with the green cells and confirm primary SDK language.
- We’ll schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive (networking, auth, deployment topology) once workbook is populated — propose Tue 2026-09-14 or Wed 2026-09-15.

Attachments: dedicated_capacity_workbook.xlsx (workbook), SLA-draft-quantica.pdf (initial), auth-patterns.md (implementation notes).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to workshop the workbook together.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Thanks Jasmine — good summary. I’ve started populating a few fields in the workbook and answered the quick items below so your team can start planning. We’ll finish the rest by Friday.

Quick answers (rough, will confirm in workbook):
- SDKs: primary is python (3.10) for backend workers; a small node (16.x) frontend service will call the API for lighter requests.
- Auth: we prefer tenant-managed API keys for startup, but want KMS integration later (compliance). Key rotation is required. Samir is CC’d for security details.
- Routing/model: prefer split path — a fast/light model for short responses (critical triage) and a high-accuracy model for long summaries. Fallback to the high-accuracy model if the fast model fails.
- Structured output: yes — function/tool calling for diagnostic extraction (JSON schema). We’ll paste one sample schema into the workbook.
- Embeddings / reranker: expected embedding writes ~45/min during index refresh; reranker QPS ~12 sustained, spikes to 30 for spikes during morning shift.
- Traffic: peak 120 requests/min, average tokens per request (input+output) ~800 tokens, target concurrent sessions ~25.
- Autoscale/queues: workable queue depth up to 60s for lower-priority batched analysis tasks; frontline triage must be sub-1s queueing.

Propose deep-dive Thu 2026-09-09 11:00am PT if that works — otherwise Tue/Wed next week.

I’ll finish the workbook and send back. Also looping Samir for comments on the KMS integration timeline.

On Wed, Sep 8, 2026 at 3:12 PM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo today, Evan — appreciate the time. Quick recap from our side and a concise list of asks so we can size Dedicated capacity and plan the technical deep-dive. I’ve attached a workbook (dedicated_capacity_workbook.xlsx) to capture the numbers below — if you can drop answers into the green cells we’ll convert them into a concrete sizing recommendation and cost estimate.

Couple of product-oriented clarifications from my side to help sizing:
- Separate pools recommendation: based on Evan’s embedding and reranker numbers we should strongly consider a separate embedding pool (CPU/GPU mix) and a small, hot reranker pool. That prevents embeddings refresh jobs from contending with low-latency generation.
- Batching: for embeddings we can batch up to 64 vectors without quality loss; recommend asynchronous writes during off-peak if possible.
- Concurrency and KV cache: for summarization flows with ~800 tokens per response, we should plan for KV cache sizing that supports 25 concurrent sessions without re-warming; that usually maps to ~2 warm GPUs (model-dependent) and autoscale to additional GPUs for peak.
- Queue policy suggestion: frontline triage route should have a strict 500ms P50 target and 2s P99 target; non-blocking batched analytics can be queued up to 60s.

I’ll draft an initial GPU-pool sketch once we have the final workbook numbers; Marissa can pick the right comp-plan for Dedicated pricing.

—Ben
